To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alternative first exon, E14, was identified in the rat prolactine receptor (PRL-R) gene, and that E14-containing Prolactin receptor ( PRL-R) mRNA was highly expressed during development in rat brain.

the expression of PRL receptor (PRLr) mRNA containing an alternative first exon, E14, is increased during postnatal development in both female and male rat brain, whereas expression of PRLr mRNA containing other first exonic sequences is not affected by postnatal development.
the expression levels of E13 and E14 containing PRLR mRNA increase during the postnatal development in the rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental changes in the expression levels of PRLRs with different first exons in rat brain.

the developmental changes in the expression levels of alternative first exons of PRLR mRNA and the effects of sex steroid hormones on the expression levels of E13-, E14-, and E15-containing mRNAs in the rat brain.
the developmental changes in the expression of the PRLR gene, and the effects of sex steroids on the expression of PRLRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PRL is an important hormone in brain function, especially in the female, and that PRLR is expressed in brain in a sexually dimorphic manner.
the expression levels of the E14 exon-containing PRLR gene increased in both female and male brains during development.
the PRLR gene has at least 3 alternative first exons and that the E14 exon is preferentially expressed in the female and in the male rat brains during development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PRLR expression in rat brain during postnatal development is regulated by the transcriptional activation and repression of the first exon, and that E14-containing PTLR mRNA expression is regulated by 17β-estrogen.
the expression of PRL receptor mRNA containing the E14 first coding exon increases during postnatal brain development, and this increase is regulated by estrogen in the female rat brain.
the E14 first-exon containing PRLR gene is expressed in the female and the male rat brains, and the expression of this gene is regulated by sex steroid hormones in the female rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression levels of E13 and E14-containing PRR mRNA are increased in the brain of the female and male rats during postnatal development.
PRLR gene is expressed in a tissue specific and developmental regulated manner, and that the expression levels of PRLRs containing different first exons change in different patterns.
PRLR mRNA containing E14 first exon is expressed at high levels in the female and in the male rat brains during postnatal development.
